The '''1953–54 DDR-Oberliga''' was the fifth season of the [[DDR-Oberliga]], the first tier of [[East German football league system|league football]] in [[East Germany]]. 

The league was contested by fifteen teams, two less than in the previous season, and [[FC Rot-Weiss Erfurt|BSG Turbine Erfurt]] won the championship. It was the first of two championships for the club, winning it the following season as well.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/ddrchamp.html |title= East Germany - List of Champions |website= [[RSSSF]] |access-date= 19 January 2016}}</ref><ref name="Meister" >{{cite web |url=https://www.dfb.de/historie/ddr-fussball/meister/ |title= DDR-Meister |website=dfb.de |publisher=[[German Football Association]] |access-date= 19 January 2016|language=de|trans-title= East German champions}}</ref>

[[Heinz Satrapa]] of [[BSG Wismut Aue]] was the league's top scorer with 21 goals.<ref name="Goal" >{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/torschuetzenkoenige/gdr-oberliga/ |title= DDDR » Oberliga » Torschützenkönige  |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 19 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=DDR-Oberliga top scorers }}</ref>

The 1953–54 season saw the best-ever average support for the Oberliga with 14,005 spectators per game.<ref name="Fuwo" />

==Table==									
The 1953–54 season saw two newly promoted clubs, [[Fortschritt Meerane]] and [[Lokomotive Leipzig|Einheit Ost Leipzig]]. The [[FDGB-Pokal]] was won by second division [[DDR-Liga]] club [[1. FC Frankfurt|ZSK Vorwärts Berlin]].<ref name="Ddr" >{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/ddrhist.html |title= East Germany 1946-1990 |website= [[RSSSF]] |access-date= 19 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/spielplan/gdr-oberliga-1953-1954-spieltag/28/ |title= DDR » Oberliga 1953/1954 |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 19 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=DDR-Oberliga 1953–54}}</ref>
